layout.heading: Great Smoky Cannabis Company vs Smoky Cannabis Company
layout.body:
Great Smoky Cannabis Company (GSCC) is the recreational cannabis dispensary on the Qualla Boundary in Cherokee, operating under the sovereignty of the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians. That Cherokee dispensary serves walk-in customers on tribal land — even though recreational cannabis remains prohibited elsewhere in North Carolina.

Smoky Cannabis Company is different. We are not GSCC, not a Smoky Mountain dispensary on the reservation, and not a Cherokee NC dispensary. Through Smoky Mountain CBD we offer hemp-derived THCa you can order online today: flower, edibles, and carefully labeled concentrates that ship from Western North Carolina.

layout.heading: Is THCa legal in North Carolina?
layout.body:
Recreational marijuana is not legalized statewide in North Carolina. The Cherokee dispensary (Great Smoky Cannabis Company) operates on tribal land under a sovereignty-based exception for in-person sales — that path is not available to everyone and is not an online store.

Hemp-derived THCa products are sold under the federal hemp framework when finished goods meet applicable delta-9 THC limits. Rules can change by product type and destination, so availability depends on current law where you live. We do not give legal advice; shop compliant hemp-derived THCa from Smoky Mountain CBD when those products are allowed in your area.

layout.heading: Does THCa get you high?
layout.lead: Raw THCa is generally described as non-intoxicating, but heating THCa can convert it into THC, which may produce an intoxicating effect. Product strength, method, dose, and individual response all matter.

layout.heading: Education, not medical advice
layout.body: This is general cannabinoid education, not a promise of effects or medical guidance. Do not drive or operate machinery after using a product that may be intoxicating. Smoky Cannabis Company is not Great Smoky Cannabis Company or the Cherokee dispensary.

layout.heading: What changes when THCa is heated?
layout.body:
THCa is the acidic form of THC found in raw hemp and cannabis flower. Heat can cause decarboxylation, a chemical change that converts THCa into THC. That is why smoking or vaporizing THCa flower may feel different from handling unheated flower. Edibles and concentrates may have their own timing and intensity considerations.

Read the label and lab information for the specific product. Never assume a product is non-intoxicating simply because it is marketed as THCa, and keep products away from children and pets.

items.question: Does THCa flower get you high when smoked?
items.answer: It can. Smoking heats THCa and can convert it into THC, which may be intoxicating. Effects vary by product and person, so use the label and do not drive after use.

items.question: Is THCa the same as THC?
items.answer: No. THCa is an acidic precursor to THC. Heating can convert THCa into THC, so the two terms should not be treated as interchangeable.

items.question: Does THCa show up on a drug test?
items.answer: A hemp-derived product may contain or produce cannabinoids that create a risk of a positive drug test. Do not use a product if you need to avoid that risk; testing methods and products vary.
